Welcome to One Line A Day. We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting it. This Privacy Policy details how we handle information in the application.\n\nLocal-First Guarantee: One Line A Day is a local-first application. All of your journal entries, selected moods, and photo attachments are stored directly and exclusively on your device. We do not operate servers, and we do not collect, transmit, share, or sell your personal data.

All data processed by the application is kept private and stored locally on your device:

• Journal Entries & Moods: Written entries and mood selections are stored in a local, encrypted-by-default SQLite database managed by the Android Room database framework.
• Photos: When you attach photos to your journal entries, the app copies the image files into its private internal application directory (filesDir). These files are inaccessible to other apps and are not uploaded to any server.
• Configuration Data: Application settings, including your dark mode preference and reminder schedules, are saved locally on the device using Android SharedPreferences and DataStore.

To support its core journaling features, the app requests the following system permissions:

• Notifications (POST_NOTIFICATIONS): Used only to deliver daily reminder alerts prompting you to write your entry. This permission is requested at runtime on supported Android versions, and you can disable reminders or permissions at any time.
• Receive Boot Completed (RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED): Used to automatically restore and reschedule your configured daily reminder notifications whenever your device is restarted.
• Microphone (RECORD_AUDIO): Used only if you choose to record voice memos to attach to your journal entries. This permission is requested at runtime and is never used without your explicit action.

The app does not request or require permissions to access your contacts, location, accounts, camera, or general external file storage directories.

The app uses a small number of open-source third-party dependencies to improve functionality:

• Coil: Used locally to load and display attached images on the screens.
• iText PDF: Used locally on your device to compile and render your journal database into a shareable PDF format.
• Google AdMob: Used to display optional rewarded video ads before PDF export. AdMob may collect device identifiers and usage data as described in Google's Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy). No personal journal data is shared with AdMob.

Coil and iText operate fully locally within the app and do not collect, store, or transmit your personal data externally.

Because all data remains strictly on your own physical device, the security of your journal relies on your device\'s overall security settings. We recommend securing your device with a PIN, pattern, password, or biometric lock to prevent unauthorized physical access to your device and journal entries.

Our application is completely safe for all users, including children. We do not collect any personal data whatsoever, making the application fully compliant with child privacy laws globally, including COPPA and GDPR.
If you have any questions, suggestions, or concerns regarding this privacy policy, feel free to contact us via email:\n\nDeveloper Support: developeraisteps@gmail.com

One Line A Day is designed as a local-first journaling application. Your journal entries, moods, tags, attached media, and voice notes are primarily stored in the app\'s private storage on your device.\n\nWe do not operate our own account or journal-sync server, and your journal content is not intentionally sent to us for advertising or analytics. However, the app uses third-party Google services for advertising and purchases, and those services may process technical device and usage information as described below.
2. Journal Data Stored on Your Device

Journal entries, moods, dates, tags, streak information, and related journal metadata are stored using Android Room and SQLite in the app's private storage.

Photos, videos, and voice recordings that you attach may also be copied into private application storage.

The application does not currently add its own database-level encryption layer to the Room database. Your device and Android operating system may provide storage encryption and other device-level protections. You can also enable App Lock inside One Line A Day to require device authentication before opening the diary.

One Line A Day uses Google Mobile Ads to display advertising, including banner, native, interstitial, and rewarded advertisements.

Google Mobile Ads may collect or share technical information such as IP address, approximate location derived from IP address, app interactions, diagnostic information, and device or advertising identifiers. This information may be used for advertising, analytics, fraud prevention, security, and related Google services.

Your journal text, journal photos, tags, and voice recordings are not intentionally supplied to Google Mobile Ads for advertising.

The app also uses Google Play Billing for optional premium purchases. Purchase processing is handled by Google Play. The app may receive purchase and entitlement information needed to determine whether premium features are available. We do not receive your full payment-card information.

Notifications: Used to provide optional daily journal reminders.

Microphone: Used only when you choose to record a voice note.

Receive Boot Completed: Used to restore scheduled reminder notifications after the device restarts.

Biometric authentication: Used when you enable App Lock so Android can authenticate you using supported device security such as biometrics, PIN, pattern, or password.

Internet and network state: Required by features such as Google Mobile Ads and Google Play services.

The app does not request general location, contacts, SMS, call log, or broad external-storage permissions.

Android system backup or device-transfer features may back up eligible application database and preference data when those features are enabled on your device or Google account.

One Line A Day also provides user-initiated export features. If you export a journal backup, PDF, image, or other file and choose another application or cloud-storage provider, that exported data will be handled by the destination you select and according to that provider's privacy practices.

We do not automatically upload your journal entries to our own cloud server.

Journal data is stored within Android application-private storage. The app also provides an optional App Lock that uses Android device authentication.\n\nNo application or security system can guarantee absolute security. You should keep your Android device protected with a PIN, password, pattern, or supported biometric authentication and keep the operating system updated.

One Line A Day is not specifically designed as a service directed at children. We do not claim that the application is automatically compliant with every child-privacy law in every country.\n\nIf the application is distributed to audiences that include children, additional Google Play Families, advertising, consent, and regional legal requirements may apply.

We may update this Privacy Policy when the application, third-party SDKs, legal requirements, or data practices change.
